glossary.Dilation: Widening of a vessel beyond its normal diameter.
glossary.Aorta: The largest artery, carrying blood from the left ventricle to the body.
glossary.Diameter: Width of a vessel measured straight across.
glossary.Atherosclerosis: Build-up of fatty plaques in artery walls causing narrowing and stiffening.
glossary.Compression symptoms: Symptoms caused by an enlarging mass pressing on nearby structures, e.g. hoarseness or difficulty swallowing.
glossary.Tachycardia: Heart rate over 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Haemodynamic: Relating to blood flow and blood pressure.
glossary.Screening: Testing people without symptoms to find disease early.
glossary.Abdominal ultrasound: Ultrasound scan of the abdomen; measures aortic diameter quickly and without radiation.
glossary.Endovascular: Done from inside the blood vessels, using catheters passed through an artery.
glossary.Stent graft: Fabric-covered metal tube placed inside the aorta to exclude the aneurysm from blood flow.
glossary.Vascular surgeon: Surgeon who treats diseases of arteries and veins.
glossary.Anaesthetic risk: Likelihood of serious complications from general anaesthesia, higher with heart or lung disease.
glossary.Comorbidities: Other medical conditions a patient has at the same time.
glossary.Perioperative mortality: Risk of death around the time of an operation.
glossary.Re-intervention: A further procedure needed to fix or maintain a previous repair.
glossary.Wall tension: The stretching force within a vessel wall; rises with pressure and radius.
glossary.Wall stress: Force per unit area acting on a vessel wall.
glossary.Chronic inflammation: Long-lasting immune activity that damages tissue over time.
glossary.Degradation: Breakdown of a structure or molecule.
glossary.Units of blood: Standard bags of donated red cells, each raising Hb by about 10 g/L.
